method: Ran the six-assertion W6 verifier and the preserved seven-assertion ERR-138 verifier. Compiled all five lesson Python fences, executed the primary demo and compared its full stdout byte-for-byte with the published text block, and executed all four functions in the published attack-test fence against the exact policy module. Reviewed current OWASP Authorization and Logging guidance, Linux cgroup v2 controller availability/enabling, and Python Popen.communicate timeout cleanup and output buffering. No provider request or external network call. The production build generated 400 pages and Pagefind indexed 400 pages/15,444 words. Captured the rendered lesson in light and dark themes at 1300px viewport width and checked article width, document overflow, Mermaid rendering, stylesheet HTTP status, and browser console.
limitations: The primary policy demo is deliberately vulnerable and its allow/deny behavior is a local teaching fixture, not evidence of production enforcement.

The final dispatch example was tested with local in-memory handlers and a synthetic audit sink; no real identity provider, durable/tamper-resistant log backend, deployed route coverage, or external side effect was exercised.

No host cgroup configuration, kernel controller, process-group/container termination, resource cap, or output cap was exercised; documentation checkpoints establish platform contract, not deployment state.
The historical prompt-injection and provider experiment summaries lack original request/response traces and remain unverified.
The browser console reported only the existing missing favicon.ico (404); the lesson stylesheet returned HTTP 200 and the page had no horizontal overflow.
